purpose: Provide a fine-grained, machine-facing knowledge base for planning, evaluating, prioritizing, and validating relevance-feedback and query-modeling methods (Rocchio, PRF, relevance models, term-dependence, click models, propensity/IPS, counterfactual evaluation, and selective-feedback control) within session-bounded heavy-LLM-assisted work.
assumptions: No observed dataset, benchmark, or expert-judgment input was supplied; all numeric values are heuristic priors.
Topic is scoped under subdomain ranking_and_relevance within domain information_retrieval.
Click-model and propensity nodes presume the availability of click logs for those branches only.
Each node is bounded to one heavy-thinking session producing a reusable handoff artifact.
exclusions: Neural dense-retrieval architecture design and training infrastructure.
Learning-to-rank feature engineering beyond term-dependence and feedback signals.
Online experimentation platform engineering and A/B governance.

competency_questions.question: Which feedback signal source (explicit, pseudo, implicit/click) does a given expansion or feedback method consume?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: answerable if REL_FEEDBACK_DEF taxonomy maps each method node to one source

competency_questions.question: How should feedback/expansion effectiveness be measured without seen-document bias?
How do explicit relevant and non-relevant documents reweight a query (Rocchio alpha/beta/gamma, negative feedback)?
How are expansion terms estimated from a pseudo-relevant set (PRF, RM1/RM3, mixture/divergence-min)?
What base scoring model do language-model feedback methods extend and how does smoothing affect them?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: answerable from QLM and its dependency edges

competency_questions.question: When should expansion use global query-independent vs local query-conditioned vs embedding-based terms?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: answerable from GLOBAL_EXPANSION, LOCAL_EXPANSION, EMBED_EXPANSION conflict axis

competency_questions.question: How do embeddings supply semantic expansion terms beyond exact co-occurrence?
How are term dependencies and proximity modeled (proximity, SDM, full MRF) and when is each justified?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: answerable from PROXIMITY, SDM, MRF and their conflict axis

competency_questions.question: How do click models separate examination from relevance (cascade, DCM, UBM, DBN)?
How is position bias / examination propensity estimated?
How are biased clicks turned into an unbiased learning signal via inverse propensity scoring?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: answerable from IPS and its dependency on POSITION_BIAS

competency_questions.question: How can a candidate ranker be evaluated offline from logged feedback with confidence bounds?
How are within-session query reformulations modeled to inform cross-turn feedback?
How should query difficulty be predicted to gate selective feedback/expansion?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: answerable from QPP and PRF_CORE/QPP conflict axis

glossary.definition: Expansion that assumes top-k initial results are relevant without user judgment.
A language model of relevance estimated from feedback documents (RM1), optionally interpolated with the query (RM3).
Vector-space query update combining original query, relevant centroid, and non-relevant centroid via alpha/beta/gamma.
Probability that a user examines a result at a given position, independent of relevance.
Reweighting observed feedback by the inverse examination propensity to obtain an unbiased estimator.
Ranking model that captures interactions among query terms beyond bag-of-words.
Estimation of per-query retrieval difficulty used to gate feedback decisions.
Off-policy estimation of a ranker's effectiveness from logged feedback of another policy.
Adding terms to a query to improve recall, from global, local, or embedding sources.
Effectiveness measurement after removing documents already shown as feedback, to avoid seen-document bias.

source_registry.description: Heuristic priors for relevance-feedback and query-modeling estimates absent observed data.

nodes.definition: Define the relevance-feedback objective: how user/pseudo/implicit relevance signals reshape a query representation to raise retrieval effectiveness.

included: explicit vs implicit vs pseudo feedback taxonomy

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a new feedback signal source (e.g., dwell, scroll) must be classified

pros.claim: Frames every downstream expansion/feedback method against one shared objective.
pros.example: Distinguishes Rocchio (explicit) from PRF (pseudo) so they are not conflated.

cons.claim: Mis-scoping feedback type propagates wrong assumptions to all expansion nodes.
cons.example: Treating pseudo-feedback as if it had true labels overstates confidence.

failure_modes: conflating implicit clicks with explicit judgments
acceptance_tests: each downstream method maps to one source
revisit_triggers: signal-source matrix contradicts a method node

nodes.definition: Apply Rocchio centroid update q'=alpha*q+beta*mean(rel)-gamma*mean(nonrel) to move the query vector toward relevant and away from non-relevant documents.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: feedback-set size or label quality changes materially

pros.claim: Simple, interpretable, strong classic baseline for explicit feedback.
pros.example: beta>gamma weighting captures positive evidence more than negative.

cons.claim: Sensitive to alpha/beta/gamma; needs judged nonrelevant set rarely available.
cons.example: High gamma can over-penalize and drift the query off-topic.

nodes.definition: Assume top-k initial results are relevant and harvest expansion terms from them without any user judgment.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: feedback depth k or first-pass retriever changes

pros.claim: No labels required; large average recall gains on many collections.
pros.example: Top-10 blind feedback expands sparse queries with co-occurring terms.

cons.claim: Query drift when top-k is non-relevant; hurts already-good queries.
cons.example: An ambiguous query pulls in off-topic terms from a wrong top result.

nodes.definition: Estimate a relevance language model RM1 from pseudo-relevant documents and interpolate it with the query (RM3) for principled PRF expansion.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: collection LM or smoothing parameter changes

pros.claim: Probabilistically grounded PRF; RM3 robustly outperforms RM1 by anchoring to the query.
pros.example: lambda interpolation keeps original query terms dominant while adding feedback terms.

cons.claim: Sensitive to document smoothing and lambda; cost of full term distributions.
cons.example: Poor smoothing inflates rare-term weights in the relevance model.

acceptance_tests: RM3 vs RM1 vs query-likelihood compared

nodes.definition: Derive expansion term weights via a mixture model that separates topical from background terms, or by divergence minimization over the feedback set.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: background model or mixing weight changes

pros.claim: Explicitly removes generic background terms, sharpening topical expansion.
pros.example: EM mixture down-weights stopword-like terms common to all docs.

cons.claim: EM convergence and mixing-weight choice add tuning burden and instability.
cons.example: Bad background weight leaves generic terms dominating expansion.

nodes.definition: Expand queries from corpus-global resources (co-occurrence thesaurus, WordNet, learned global term associations) independent of the result set.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: global resource refreshed or replaced

pros.claim: Stable, query-independent expansions usable when no good first pass exists.
pros.example: Synonym from thesaurus helps a single-term query with no feedback docs.

cons.claim: Ignores query context; injects wrong senses and ambiguous synonyms.
cons.example: 'bank' expands with both finance and river terms regardless of intent.

nodes.definition: Expand from the result-set-local context (local context analysis, passage-level co-occurrence) so expansions are query-conditioned.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: passage windowing or first-pass retriever changes

pros.claim: Query-conditioned terms reduce sense ambiguity vs global expansion.
pros.example: Local passages around query terms pick the intended sense of 'jaguar'.

cons.claim: Inherits first-pass errors; passage windowing adds parameters.
cons.example: A bad top result seeds locally-coherent but off-topic expansion.

nodes.definition: Select expansion terms or pseudo-query vectors via embedding nearest neighbors (word2vec/contextual), optionally averaging or generative PRF.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: embedding model or vocabulary changes

pros.claim: Captures semantic neighbors missed by exact co-occurrence.
pros.example: Embedding kNN adds 'automobile' for query 'car' without a thesaurus.

cons.claim: Embedding neighbors can be topically loose; domain shift hurts static vectors.
cons.example: Nearest neighbor of 'apple' mixes fruit and company senses.

nodes.definition: Score documents by the probability they generate the query under a smoothed document language model, the base model many feedback methods extend.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: smoothing method or collection statistics change

pros.claim: Principled base enabling RM3 and divergence-min feedback to plug in.
pros.example: Dirichlet smoothing gives stable estimates feeding RM1 expansion.

cons.claim: Smoothing choice strongly affects downstream feedback quality.
cons.example: Wrong mu in Dirichlet smoothing destabilizes relevance-model terms.

nodes.definition: Reward documents where query terms appear close together (spans, distance kernels), capturing weak ordering beyond bag-of-words.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: proximity kernel or window retuned

pros.claim: Cheap precision gain by rewarding co-located query terms.
pros.example: Documents with 'machine learning' adjacent outrank scattered matches.

cons.claim: Kernel/window choice is collection-dependent and adds parameters.
cons.example: Too-wide window makes proximity indistinguishable from bag-of-words.

nodes.definition: Apply the MRF sequential-dependence model weighting unigram, ordered-bigram, and unordered-window features with fixed mixing weights.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: SDM weights retuned or query type shifts

pros.claim: Strong, robust term-dependence baseline with only three weights.
pros.example: Default 0.85/0.10/0.05 SDM weights reliably beat unigram QL.

cons.claim: Fixed weights are a compromise; ignores variable dependence strength.
cons.example: Phrasal queries underweight ordered bigrams under default weights.

nodes.definition: Model term dependencies as an MRF over cliques (full dependence), generalizing SDM to arbitrary term interactions.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: clique feature set or weighting method changes

pros.claim: General framework subsuming SDM and full dependence variants.
pros.example: Full-dependence cliques capture multi-term concepts SDM omits.

cons.claim: Full dependence explodes feature count with marginal gains and high tuning cost.
cons.example: All-subset cliques on long queries become intractable to weight.

nodes.definition: Model the probability a user clicks a result as a function of relevance and examination, via cascade, DCM, UBM, or DBN families.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: presentation layout or click-behavior regime changes

pros.claim: Disentangle examination from relevance, turning biased clicks into usable signal.
pros.example: DBN separates attractiveness from satisfaction across a session.

cons.claim: Model-misspecification risk; sparse tail queries get unstable estimates.
cons.example: Cascade model breaks when users click multiple results per query.

acceptance_tests: model family justified per traffic pattern

nodes.definition: Estimate the examination/position propensity curve (RandomizationEM, intervention harvesting, regression-EM) needed to debias clicks.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: logging/ranking policy that generated clicks changes

pros.claim: Propensities are the prerequisite for IPS-based unbiased learning.
pros.example: Estimated examination curve lets clicks be reweighted by 1/propensity.

cons.claim: Hard to estimate without interventions; errors propagate into every IPS estimate.
cons.example: Underestimated tail propensities inflate IPS variance massively.

acceptance_tests: sensitivity of IPS to propensity error checked

nodes.definition: Reweight observed click feedback by inverse examination propensity to obtain an unbiased estimator of relevance/utility.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: propensity estimates or clipping threshold change

pros.claim: Provably unbiased under correct propensities; standard for unbiased LTR.
pros.example: Self-normalized IPS controls variance from tiny tail propensities.

cons.claim: High variance under small/wrong propensities; bias-variance tradeoff via clipping.
cons.example: Unclipped IPS on rare positions yields exploding gradient estimates.

nodes.definition: Estimate how a new ranker would have performed from logged feedback using IPS/doubly-robust off-policy estimators, with confidence bounds.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: logging policy or candidate-policy divergence changes

pros.claim: Screens candidate rankers offline before risky online tests.
pros.example: DR estimator gives a CI on NDCG lift before launching an A/B.

cons.claim: Invalid under poor logging-policy overlap; over-trusted estimates mislead launches.
cons.example: No support overlap makes the off-policy estimate meaningless.

revisit_triggers: candidate policy far from logging policy

nodes.definition: Model within-session query reformulations (add/remove/substitute terms, intent shifts) to inform feedback and expansion across turns.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: session segmentation or carryover policy changes

pros.claim: Captures evolving intent that single-query feedback ignores.
pros.example: Carrying terms from a refined query improves the next turn's recall.

cons.claim: Session boundary and intent-shift detection are noisy.
cons.example: A topic switch mid-session wrongly carries stale terms forward.

nodes.definition: Predict per-query retrieval difficulty pre- or post-retrieval (clarity, NQC, WIG) to gate whether feedback/expansion should be applied.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: predictor or gating threshold retuned

pros.claim: Enables selective feedback, avoiding drift on already-good queries.
pros.example: Low predicted difficulty skips PRF to protect a precise query.

cons.claim: Predictors correlate weakly with true difficulty on some collections.
cons.example: Clarity score mis-ranks difficulty for very short queries.

nodes.definition: Use explicitly non-relevant documents to push the query away from off-topic regions, the hardest feedback regime (difficult/diverse topics).

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: negative feedback aggregation strategy changes

pros.claim: Only reliable lever for very hard/ambiguous topics where positives are scarce.
pros.example: Removing a dominant wrong sense via negatives rescues a hard query.

cons.claim: Single negative centroid is unstable; non-relevant set is heterogeneous.
cons.example: One negative centroid cannot represent multiple distinct off-topic clusters.

failure_modes: heterogeneous nonrel set collapsed to one centroid

nodes.definition: Define the residual-collection / per-query risk-reward protocol and metrics that fairly measure feedback and expansion effectiveness.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: evaluation protocol or metric set changes

pros.claim: Prevents the seen-document bias and mean-metric blindness that overstate feedback gains.
pros.example: Residual collection removes judged feedback docs before scoring.

cons.claim: Residual evaluation and per-query reporting add overhead and judgment needs.
cons.example: Reporting only mean AP hides that feedback hurt 30% of queries.

edges.why_related: Feedback-type framing must precede explicit Rocchio so it targets the right signal source.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Correct signal typing prevents misuse of explicit-feedback math.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Rocchio applied to pseudo signals if framing skipped.
edges.example: Rocchio uses explicit judgments defined by the framing node.
edges.resolution_rule: framing dominates; Rocchio config must cite the feedback-type taxonomy.

edges.why_related: Pseudo-feedback assumption is only valid once the feedback taxonomy distinguishes pseudo from explicit.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Prevents treating blind feedback as labeled data.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Overstated confidence on unlabeled top-k.
edges.example: PRF declared as pseudo source in the taxonomy before use.
edges.resolution_rule: framing dominates.

edges.why_related: RM1/RM3 estimate the relevance model from the pseudo-relevant set produced by PRF.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Reuses PRF set selection for principled term weighting.
edges.risk_of_conflict: RM built on a bad pseudo set inherits drift.
edges.example: RM1 consumes the top-k set chosen by PRF_CORE.
edges.resolution_rule: upstream PRF set quality dominates RM estimation.

edges.why_related: RM3 interpolates with and is scored under the query-likelihood LM, so QLM must exist first.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Shared smoothing/LM machinery.
edges.risk_of_conflict: RM term weights unstable without consistent smoothing.
edges.example: RM3 query model is plugged into the QLM scorer.
edges.resolution_rule: QLM smoothing config dominates RM estimation.

edges.why_related: Mixture/divergence-min variants operate on the same pseudo-relevant set as core PRF.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Cleaner topical terms from the same feedback set.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Background suppression on a bad set still drifts.
edges.example: EM mixture estimated over the PRF top-k set.
edges.resolution_rule: PRF set selection dominates.

edges.why_related: Mixture/divergence-min models are defined relative to the collection/background LM from QLM.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Consistent background model.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Inconsistent background inflates generic terms.
edges.example: Background model reused from QLM smoothing.
edges.resolution_rule: QLM background definition dominates.

edges.why_related: Global expansion is a feedback-free path that the framing node positions against local methods.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Clarifies when query-independent expansion is appropriate.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Used where local feedback was the right tool.
edges.example: Framing labels global expansion as feedback-independent.
edges.resolution_rule: framing dominates routing.

edges.why_related: Local expansion draws terms from the pseudo-relevant result set produced by PRF.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Query-conditioned terms from existing top-k.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Inherits first-pass errors from PRF.
edges.example: Local context analysis runs over PRF top results.
edges.resolution_rule: PRF set quality dominates local expansion.

edges.why_related: Embedding expansion extends local result-conditioned selection with semantic neighbors.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Adds semantic recall on top of local terms.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Semantic neighbors loosen an already-local set.
edges.example: Embedding kNN reranks local candidate terms.
edges.resolution_rule: local conditioning dominates neighbor selection.

edges.why_related: Embedding expansion must respect the feedback-source typing from the framing node.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Keeps embedding expansion mapped to a defined source.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Untyped embedding expansion mixes signal sources.
edges.example: Embedding expansion declared against a feedback source.
edges.resolution_rule: framing dominates.

edges.why_related: SDM's ordered/unordered window features build directly on proximity scoring.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Reuses positional proximity machinery.
edges.risk_of_conflict: SDM windows wrong if proximity index missing.
edges.example: SDM unordered-window feature is a proximity kernel.
edges.resolution_rule: proximity feature availability dominates.

edges.why_related: MRF clique potentials generalize proximity features into the dependence framework.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Unifies proximity into a learnable model.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Clique features meaningless without proximity primitives.
edges.example: MRF clique uses proximity-based potentials.
edges.resolution_rule: proximity primitives dominate clique design.

edges.why_related: SDM is a fixed-weight special case of the MRF, so the MRF framework precedes it conceptually.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: SDM inherits MRF's clique semantics.
edges.risk_of_conflict: SDM weights misread without MRF grounding.
edges.example: SDM = MRF restricted to sequential cliques.
edges.resolution_rule: MRF formalism dominates SDM specialization.

edges.why_related: Proximity features are combined with the base QLM score.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Adds positional signal to the base scorer.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Proximity weight mis-set vs base score.
edges.example: Proximity score is a feature added to QLM.
edges.resolution_rule: QLM base scoring dominates feature mixing.

edges.why_related: Click models are an implicit-feedback source the framing node must classify before use.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Maps clicks to the implicit-feedback branch.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Clicks treated as explicit labels if unframed.
edges.example: Click models declared as implicit feedback source.
edges.resolution_rule: framing dominates click-signal typing.

edges.why_related: Position-bias estimation factors examination out of the click model, so the click model precedes it.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Shared examination/relevance decomposition.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Propensities meaningless without a click model.
edges.example: Propensity curve estimated from click-model examination factor.
edges.resolution_rule: click-model structure dominates propensity estimation.

edges.why_related: IPS reweights clicks by inverse propensity, so propensities must be estimated first.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Turns biased clicks into an unbiased signal.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Wrong propensities make IPS unusable.
edges.example: IPS divides each click by its examination propensity.
edges.resolution_rule: propensity quality dominates IPS validity.

edges.why_related: Counterfactual evaluation uses IPS (and DR) estimators to score candidate policies offline.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Reuses IPS weights for off-policy estimates.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Off-policy estimate inherits IPS variance.
edges.example: Off-policy NDCG estimated via IPS-weighted logged clicks.
edges.resolution_rule: IPS estimator validity dominates eval validity.

edges.why_related: Negative feedback extends the Rocchio negative-centroid term to hard-topic regimes.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Reuses Rocchio's gamma machinery.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Negative centroid unstable without Rocchio base.
edges.example: Negative feedback is the gamma term of Rocchio emphasized.
edges.resolution_rule: Rocchio formulation dominates negative-feedback design.

edges.why_related: Post-retrieval QPP predictors read the QLM score distribution to predict difficulty.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Reuses first-pass scores for gating.
edges.risk_of_conflict: QPP gates on a noisy score distribution.
edges.example: Clarity/NQC computed from QLM result scores.
edges.resolution_rule: QLM scoring dominates QPP inputs.

edges.why_related: A fair evaluation protocol should be fixed before tuning Rocchio to avoid optimizing to a biased metric.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Stops over-fitting to seen documents.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Rocchio tuned against a biased metric.
edges.example: Residual-collection protocol set before alpha/beta/gamma search.
edges.resolution_rule: evaluation protocol precedes tuning.

edges.why_related: Evaluation protocol must precede PRF tuning so gains are measured without seen-document bias.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Prevents inflated PRF gains.
edges.risk_of_conflict: PRF depth tuned to a biased metric.
edges.example: Residual evaluation set before PRF depth sweep.
edges.resolution_rule: evaluation protocol precedes PRF tuning.

edges.why_related: QPP should gate whether PRF is applied, so its prediction precedes the PRF decision.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Selective feedback avoids drift on easy queries.
edges.risk_of_conflict: PRF applied where QPP would have skipped it.
edges.example: Low predicted difficulty skips PRF expansion.
edges.resolution_rule: QPP gating precedes PRF application.

edges.why_related: Session reformulation context should inform local expansion term carryover across turns.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Cross-turn terms enrich local expansion.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Stale session terms pollute expansion.
edges.example: Carried session terms seed next-turn local expansion.
edges.resolution_rule: reformulation state precedes carryover.

edges.why_related: PRF design changes the per-query risk-reward distribution the evaluation must capture.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Reveals which queries feedback helps or harms.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Mean-only eval hides PRF-induced harm.
edges.example: Aggressive PRF raises mean AP but lowers robustness index.
edges.resolution_rule: report per-query risk-reward when PRF changes.

edges.why_related: Propensity-estimation error changes the bias and variance of counterfactual estimates.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Better propensities tighten off-policy CIs.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Propensity error silently biases the estimate.
edges.example: Underestimated propensities inflate counterfactual NDCG variance.
edges.resolution_rule: gate eval on propensity confidence intervals.

edges.why_related: Semantic expansion changes recall/precision tradeoff that the metric set must reflect.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Surfaces recall gains from semantic terms.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Precision-only metric penalizes recall gains.
edges.example: Embedding expansion lifts recall but mean P@10 drops.
edges.resolution_rule: choose metrics that credit recall when embedding expansion is used.

edges.why_related: Poor evaluated effectiveness of RM3 triggers revisiting smoothing/lambda choices.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Closes the loop between eval and RM tuning.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Endless retuning without a stop rule.
edges.example: Low robustness index re-opens RM3 lambda search.
edges.resolution_rule: revisit RM3 only if eval delta exceeds threshold; stop after max 3 retunes.

edges.why_related: Evaluation discrepancies between offline clicks and judgments trigger click-model re-selection.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Aligns click model with observed behavior.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Repeated click-model swaps without convergence.
edges.example: Offline/online disagreement re-opens click-model family choice.
edges.resolution_rule: revisit click model only on material disagreement; stop after 2 swaps.

edges.why_related: Unstable counterfactual estimates trigger revisiting IPS clipping/variance-reduction settings.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Tightens estimator variance.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Clipping retuned indefinitely.
edges.example: Wide off-policy CI re-opens IPS clipping threshold.
edges.resolution_rule: revisit IPS clipping only if CI width exceeds gate; max 3 iterations.

edges.why_related: Blanket PRF maximizes mean recall while QPP-based selective feedback withholds expansion to protect precision.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Balances recall gains vs drift protection.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Blind expansion drifts; over-gating loses recall.
edges.example: QPP says skip but PRF expands anyway, drifting an easy query.
edges.resolution_rule: QPP gating dominates: apply PRF only when predicted difficulty exceeds threshold.

edges.why_related: Global query-independent expansion and local query-conditioned expansion pull term selection in opposite directions.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Coverage vs context-precision tradeoff.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Wrong-sense global terms vs first-pass-biased local terms.
edges.example: Global adds both senses of 'bank'; local picks one but may be wrong.
edges.resolution_rule: prefer local when first pass is reliable (QPP-easy); else fall back to global.

edges.why_related: Full-dependence MRF maximizes expressiveness while SDM minimizes parameters for robustness.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Expressiveness vs robustness/tuning-cost tradeoff.
edges.risk_of_conflict: MRF overfits; SDM underfits phrasal queries.
edges.example: Full cliques help long queries but explode feature count vs SDM's three weights.
edges.resolution_rule: default to SDM; escalate to full MRF only with evidence of phrasal under-modeling.

edges.why_related: Implicit IPS-debiased signals and explicit negative judgments can disagree on what is non-relevant.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Combines implicit and explicit evidence.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Implicit non-click contradicts explicit non-relevance label.
edges.example: A non-clicked result is explicitly judged relevant, conflicting signals.
edges.resolution_rule: explicit negative judgments dominate implicit non-clicks when both exist.

edges.why_related: Click-derived effectiveness signals and judgment-based residual evaluation can disagree on system quality.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Cross-checks online vs offline signals.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Optimizing clicks degrades judged relevance.
edges.example: CTR rises while judged NDCG falls due to clickbait titles.
edges.resolution_rule: judged residual evaluation dominates for relevance claims; clicks inform engagement only.

edges.why_related: Both reweight the query from a feedback set but in vector vs language-model space.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Cross-paradigm dedup and method selection.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Confusing the two paradigms in tuning.
edges.example: Rocchio centroid and RM relevance model both add feedback terms.
edges.resolution_rule: keep separate; choose by retrieval model (vector vs LM).

edges.why_related: Both add query-independent semantic terms (lexical resource vs embedding space).
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Helps decide which semantic resource to use.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Double-expanding with overlapping terms.
edges.example: Thesaurus synonyms overlap embedding neighbors.
edges.resolution_rule: prefer embeddings when a domain-matched model exists; else thesaurus.

conflict_axes.trigger: feedback applied to queries with non-relevant top-k
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: Apply expansion only when QPP predicts difficulty above threshold; otherwise protect precision.
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: per-query harm rate > 0.30 in residual evaluation
conflict_axes.example: Aggressive PRF lifts mean AP but hurts 35% of easy queries.

conflict_axes.trigger: choosing an expansion source for an ambiguous query
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: Prefer local/embedding when first pass is reliable; fall back to global when no usable feedback set exists.
conflict_axes.example: Global adds both senses of 'bank'; local disambiguates but may be off-topic.

conflict_axes.dominance_logic: Default to SDM; escalate to full MRF only with evidence of phrasal under-modeling.
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: clique count growth makes weighting intractable
conflict_axes.example: Full cliques help long queries but explode features vs SDM's three weights.

conflict_axes.trigger: implicit and explicit signals disagree on relevance
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: Explicit judgments dominate implicit click signals when both exist for relevance claims.
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: sign disagreement on > 0.25 of overlapping items
conflict_axes.example: A non-clicked result is explicitly judged relevant.

conflict_axes.trigger: optimizing clicks diverges from judged relevance
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: Judged residual evaluation dominates relevance claims; clicks inform engagement only.
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: CTR up while judged NDCG down
conflict_axes.example: Clickbait titles raise CTR while NDCG falls.

conflict_axes.trigger: small or uncertain propensities inflate IPS variance
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: Clip propensities or use self-normalized/DR estimators when variance exceeds gate, accepting small bias.
conflict_axes.example: Unclipped IPS on rare positions yields exploding variance.

conflict_axes.trigger: choosing a feedback paradigm for the underlying retrieval model
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: Match feedback paradigm to the base retrieval model: LM feedback for LM scoring, Rocchio for vector scoring.
conflict_axes.example: Rocchio applied on top of a language-model retriever.

conflict_axes.trigger: deciding whether to apply feedback to every query
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: Selective gating via QPP dominates blanket feedback when predictor reliability is established.
conflict_axes.example: Blanket PRF expands an easy query QPP would have skipped.

edge_cases.trigger: a method references a non-existent dependency node
edge_cases.example: RM1_RM3 lists a removed node as a dependency
edge_cases.detection_method: resolve every dependency/evidence ref against node and source registries

edge_cases.trigger: PRF applied without per-query risk reporting
edge_cases.failure_mode: query drift hidden by mean metric
edge_cases.example: Mean AP rises while 35% of queries regress
edge_cases.detection_method: compare per-query baseline vs feedback ranks in residual collection

edge_cases.trigger: propensities estimated without intervention or CIs
edge_cases.example: Tail propensities underestimated, IPS variance explodes
edge_cases.detection_method: check propensity confidence intervals and IPS variance sensitivity

edge_cases.trigger: candidate policy has poor support overlap with logging policy
edge_cases.example: No support overlap makes off-policy NDCG meaningless
edge_cases.detection_method: run support/overlap diagnostic before trusting estimate

edge_cases.trigger: feedback docs left in the evaluation pool
edge_cases.example: Rocchio scored on documents it was given as feedback
edge_cases.detection_method: verify residual collection removed judged feedback documents

edge_cases.trigger: context-free global expansion injects wrong word sense
edge_cases.example: 'bank' expanded with river terms for a finance query
edge_cases.detection_method: sample expansion terms and check sense alignment to query intent

edge_cases.trigger: full-dependence cliques enumerated on long queries
edge_cases.example: All-subset cliques on an 8-term query become intractable
edge_cases.detection_method: bound clique-set size and monitor feature count vs query length

edge_cases.trigger: click-derived value labeled observed without logs
edge_cases.example: A click-model parameter labeled observed with no log supplied
edge_cases.detection_method: verify no observed/experimentally_validated labels without supplied data

edge_cases.trigger: a recall-vs-drift tradeoff encoded as a dependency
edge_cases.example: QPP-PRF tension wrongly modeled as a prerequisite
edge_cases.detection_method: check that tradeoff pressures are conflict edges, not dependency edges

edge_cases.trigger: a derived score edited without recomputation
edge_cases.example: posterior_importance edited but PI*EC not recomputed
edge_cases.detection_method: recompute final_importance/risk/edge_priority and compare within tolerance

edge_cases.trigger: eval-driven retuning loop lacks a stop condition
edge_cases.example: RM3 lambda retuned indefinitely on tiny eval deltas
edge_cases.detection_method: verify feedback edges declare materiality threshold and max iterations

edge_cases.trigger: a high-coupling foundation hard-locked before validation
edge_cases.example: Feedback framing hard-locked before downstream methods validated
edge_cases.detection_method: verify no hard_lock before dependency, validation, and human-review gates pass

workflow.objective: Fix feedback-source taxonomy and the bias-free evaluation protocol
acceptance_tests: framing maps each method to one source
workflow.do_first_because: high-coupling, high-irreversibility foundations must stabilize before any method is tuned

workflow.objective: Establish the base retrieval/scoring model and smoothing
acceptance_tests: base scorer produces stable ranked lists
exit_criteria: base scorer validated on sample queries
workflow.do_first_because: downstream LM feedback and proximity features all extend the base scorer

exit_criteria: explicit feedback evaluated on residual collection
workflow.do_first_because: explicit feedback is the interpretable baseline the pseudo methods are compared against

workflow.objective: Implement pseudo-relevance feedback and relevance models
acceptance_tests: RM3 vs RM1 vs QL compared on residual collection
exit_criteria: pseudo-feedback gains validated without seen-doc bias
workflow.do_first_because: PRF depends on the base scorer and feeds the term-selection comparison

workflow.objective: Compare global, local, and embedding expansion sources
acceptance_tests: global vs local vs embedding ablation run
exit_criteria: best expansion source selected per query class
workflow.do_first_because: expansion sources reuse the pseudo-feedback set and must be compared before locking expansion policy
term dependence extends the base scorer and is independent of the feedback branch

workflow.objective: Fit click models and estimate position bias
workflow.do_first_because: click modeling and propensity estimation are prerequisites for any unbiased learning

workflow.objective: Apply IPS and counterfactual offline evaluation
exit_criteria: candidate ranker screened offline before online test
workflow.do_first_because: counterfactual decisions are high-risk and irreversible-leaning, requiring human review before launch

workflow.objective: Model session reformulations for cross-turn feedback
workflow.do_first_because: session modeling enriches expansion but is not a prerequisite for single-query methods

workflow.objective: Add query performance prediction to gate selective feedback
workflow.do_first_because: QPP gating depends on first-pass scores and the feedback methods it gates

workflow.objective: Consolidate fair evaluation, resolve conflicts, and gate locks
entry_criteria: all method branches drafted and validated
exit_criteria: KB ready for handoff with documented locks
workflow.do_first_because: final consolidation must not hard-lock anything before validation and human review gates pass

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-risk method conflicts with delivery speed
dominance_rules.rule: Risk-if-wrong dominates speed for IPS/counterfactual decisions.
dominance_rules.required_action: run acceptance tests and human review before launch
dominance_rules.example: Skip launch when off-policy CI is too wide even under deadline.

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-value node lacks its prerequisite
dominance_rules.rule: Dependency precedence dominates raw value ordering.
dominance_rules.required_action: schedule prerequisites first regardless of value
dominance_rules.example: RM3 waits for QLM even though RM3 has higher final_importance.

dominance_rules.trigger: a precise number lacks evidence support
dominance_rules.required_action: label estimates heuristic; never invent observed values
dominance_rules.example: A click-model parameter must stay heuristic without logs.

dominance_rules.trigger: a node is ready to lock but tests are incomplete
dominance_rules.required_action: block hard_lock until acceptance tests pass
dominance_rules.example: Counterfactual node stays draft until overlap diagnostic passes.

dominance_rules.trigger: an irreversible launch decision is reached
dominance_rules.rule: Human review dominates automation for irreversible decisions.

dominance_rules.trigger: adding nodes would break schema consistency
dominance_rules.required_action: reject near-duplicate nodes that only inflate counts
dominance_rules.example: Do not split SDM into trivial near-duplicates to hit a target.

dominance_rules.trigger: output formatting conflicts with JSON validity
dominance_rules.rule: Strict JSON validity dominates prose quality.
dominance_rules.required_action: emit valid JSON only, no markdown
dominance_rules.example: Drop explanatory prose that would break JSON.

dominance_rules.required_action: cite SRC_HEURISTIC_PRIOR for every heuristic estimate
dominance_rules.example: Every heuristic metric references the heuristic prior source.

dominance_rules.trigger: explicit judgment conflicts with implicit click signal
dominance_rules.rule: Explicit judgments dominate implicit click signals for relevance claims.
dominance_rules.required_action: prefer judged labels; use clicks for engagement only
override_requires: evaluation evidence that clicks better reflect intent
dominance_rules.example: A judged-relevant non-clicked result is treated as relevant.

dominance_rules.trigger: local optimization would reorder validated foundations
dominance_rules.example: Do not tune expansion before the evaluation protocol is fixed.

anti_rework_rules.rule: Fix the feedback-source taxonomy before tuning any method.
anti_rework_rules.rationale: Misclassified signals propagate to every method.
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a method consumes a signal type not in the taxonomy
anti_rework_rules.example: Rocchio tuned before pseudo vs explicit is defined.

anti_rework_rules.rule: Fix the bias-free evaluation protocol before tuning feedback.
anti_rework_rules.rationale: Tuning to a biased metric overstates gains.
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: gains reported on a pool containing feedback documents
anti_rework_rules.example: PRF depth tuned against seen-document-biased AP.

anti_rework_rules.rule: Establish the base scorer before language-model feedback.
anti_rework_rules.rationale: Feedback term weights depend on consistent smoothing.
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: RM terms estimated with inconsistent smoothing
anti_rework_rules.example: RM3 built before QLM smoothing is fixed.

anti_rework_rules.rule: Produce the pseudo-relevant set before local/embedding expansion.
anti_rework_rules.rationale: Local expansion reuses the PRF set.
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: local expansion run without a defined feedback set
anti_rework_rules.example: Embedding expansion seeded from an undefined top-k.

anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: IPS weights computed with no propensity model
anti_rework_rules.example: IPS reweighting before position bias estimated.

anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: off-policy CI reported without IPS variance check
anti_rework_rules.example: Counterfactual NDCG trusted on unstable IPS.

anti_rework_rules.rule: Identify conflict axes before writing dominance rules.
anti_rework_rules.rationale: Dominance rules need the conflicts they resolve.
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a dominance rule with no matching conflict axis
anti_rework_rules.example: Writing a recall-vs-drift rule before the axis exists.

anti_rework_rules.rule: Pass acceptance tests before any hard lock.
anti_rework_rules.rationale: Hard-locking unvalidated artifacts forces costly reopen.

anti_rework_rules.rule: Require human review before irreversible launch decisions.
anti_rework_rules.example: Online deployment from off-policy estimate alone.

anti_rework_rules.rule: Finalize the glossary before final node deduplication.
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: two nodes share a glossary term as their core concept
anti_rework_rules.example: RM1/RM3 and Rocchio merged without glossary check.

action: sort defects by risk and severity
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: queue empty or only sub-threshold low-risk defects

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect touches a high-coupling node
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: impact set stable across a pass

iteration_protocol.detection: apply repair routed to owning subsystem
detect upstream change to locked artifact
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: no upstream changes to locked nodes
human decision recorded for all escalations

test_cases.input_summary: single feedback method with no observed data

version_increment_rules: any hard_lock change requires version increment
schema field change requires version increment
lock_downgrade_rules: upstream dependency change downgrades dependent locks to draft
failed revalidation downgrades soft_lock to draft
